name: PORTAL POINT Ebisu
card: A community lounge in Yebisu Garden Place, flooded with light through a glass atrium
title: PORTAL POINT Ebisu — a creative office in Yebisu Garden Place, with a light-filled lounge and a nap room
lead: PORTAL POINT Ebisu is inside Glass Square at Yebisu Garden Place. It is a five-minute walk from the East Exit of JR Ebisu Station, and the Ebisu Skywalk moving walkway links the station directly to its basement level. The building, completed in 2002, was renovated in 2019. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: JR Yamanote Line Ebisu Station East Exit, 5 min walk / Tokyo Metro Hibiya Line Ebisu Station Exit 1, 12 min
Offices / shop / showroom / event space / free desks
Community lounge / nap room / event space / phone booths
concept: Light, coffee and a nap room
The official website describes “a community lounge flooded with light through a glass atrium — where you turn over new ideas with coffee in hand, and restore body and mind in the nap room”.
It covers 2,549.84 m² and combines offices with a shop, showroom and event space.
steps: The lounge is lit by light pouring through a glass atrium.
The official website presents it as a place to think up new ideas with a coffee in hand. Free desks are also available as a plan.
The official website suggests using the nap room to “restore body and mind”.
Phone booths are available for online meetings.
A place to show your work too
With showroom and event-space functions, it is a place to share your work as well as to do it.
Offices come in units from one person (15.25–121.87 m²).

word.title: What is the Ebisu Skywalk?
body: A moving walkway linking JR Ebisu Station with Yebisu Garden Place.
PORTAL POINT Ebisu's official website says that, using this walkway, you reach its basement level directly from the station.

credits: PORTAL POINT official website: “PORTAL POINT Ebisu” / Real Gate official website: WORKS

name: LIBPORT Shinagawa
card: Coworking with a view of a bamboo grove and a café next door, five minutes from the Konan Exit
title: LIBPORT Shinagawa — coworking overlooking a bamboo grove, with hanging-chair nap spots and a café next door
lead: LIBPORT Shinagawa is on the 2nd floor of the W Building in Konan 1-chome, a five-minute walk from the Konan Exit of Shinagawa Station. Across two floors, West and East, are a spacious coworking area, 20 private rooms and meeting rooms. The official website describes it as “a comfortable space near Sony's head office, overlooking a bamboo grove”. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: Shinagawa Station Konan Exit, 5 min walk
Mon–Sat 7:30–23:00 (closed Sundays, holidays and New Year) / drop-in weekdays 9:00–23:00 (last entry 17:30)
Two floors, West and East / coworking area / 20 private rooms / meeting rooms
concept: A place to refresh heart, body and mind
LIBPORT's official website describes the brand as “a place to refresh your heart, body and mind” — somewhere to switch gears when work gets stuck.
Shinagawa is described as offering “a range of plans, from a spacious coworking area to project rooms of up to 20 tsubo (about 66 m²)”.
steps: The coworking area spreads across the West and East floors.
A café next door and bamboo outside the window
The official website describes a comfortable space overlooking a bamboo grove.
A nap space with hanging chairs lets you rest before getting back to work.
There are also meeting rooms, phone booths and a multifunction printer.

word.title: What is drop-in?
body: Using a coworking space by the hour for just one day, without becoming a member.
At LIBPORT Shinagawa, drop-in is available on weekdays from 9:00 to 23:00 (last entry 17:30).

name: LIBPORT Hamamatsucho
card: A 24-hour workspace with a monorail view, 20 seconds from Hamamatsucho Station
title: LIBPORT Hamamatsucho — a 24-hour workspace 20 seconds from the station, with a view of the monorail
lead: LIBPORT Hamamatsucho is a one-minute walk from Hamamatsucho Station — “20 seconds from the station”, in the official website's words. In a building with one basement level and seven floors above ground, it has 12 free-address seats, 28 private rooms, three web-meeting booths, a phone box and two meeting rooms. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: 24 hours, every day / drop-in weekdays 9:00–23:00 (last entry 17:30)
12 free-address seats / 28 private rooms / 3 web-meeting booths / 1 phone box / 2 meeting rooms (6 people)
concept: 20 seconds from the station, 24 hours a day
The official website describes LIBPORT Hamamatsucho as “a workspace 20 seconds from the station where you can work freely, available 24 hours”.
The brand idea is “a place to refresh your heart, body and mind”. Hamamatsucho has a viewing space overlooking the monorail and a lounge exclusively for Premium Room users.
steps: Coworking members can use the 12 free-address seats.
Drop-in starts at ¥550 per hour, on weekdays from 9:00 to 23:00.
The official website features a viewing space overlooking the monorail.
Premium Room users have their own lounge, and there is also a nap space.
The viewing space overlooking the monorail
The lounge for Premium Room users
There are 28 private rooms, plus three web-meeting booths and a phone box.
There are two meeting rooms for 6, and storage rooms are available too.

word.title: What is address membership?
body: One of LIBPORT's price plans.
The official website lists it alongside coworking membership, room membership and drop-in (¥35,200 a month at Hamamatsucho).

name: BLINK Roppongi
card: Right by Roppongi Hills, a five-floor coworking space with a café lounge that feels “just like being abroad”
title: BLINK Roppongi — coworking that feels “just like being abroad”, with a ground-floor café lounge and workspaces from B1F to 4F
lead: BLINK Roppongi is in Moto-Azabu 3-chome, a two-minute walk from the WEST WALK entrance of Roppongi Hills. The official website calls it “a coworking space that feels just like being abroad”. Across five floors, from the basement to the 4th floor, are a café lounge, open desks, private offices and meeting rooms. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: Hibiya & Oedo lines Roppongi Station Exit 1a, 6 min walk / Namboku & Oedo lines Azabu-Juban Station Exits 4 & 7, 10 min
B1F–4F: café lounge / open desks / private offices (2–16 people) / meeting rooms / phone booths
concept: Coworking that feels just like being abroad
The official website says you can enjoy proper coffee in an international café, and that more than 200 events a year are held, covering business, lifestyle, music, art and more.
It is dog-friendly too — a place to work in a relaxed, unbuttoned atmosphere.
steps: A café open to non-members too
The ground floor holds the café lounge, event space and open desks. The official website says “members, of course, and non-members too can use it freely”.
There is a food menu as well as drinks.
Fixed desks and a thinking room
The basement has private offices and fixed desks available 24 hours, with meeting rooms and phone booths.
The 2nd floor has meeting rooms for 4–6, open desks and a thinking room for giving your mind a rest.
The 3rd and 4th floors hold private offices that companies can use as a 24-hour base. They are fully private, from rooms for 2 to rooms for 16.
The kitchen in the 4th-floor pantry is free to use.

word.title: What is the thinking room?
body: The name of a room on the 2nd floor of BLINK Roppongi.
The official website says “when you want to refresh your mind, you can spend some unhurried time in the thinking room”.

credits: © Blink Japan G.K. (BLINK COMMUNITY official website: “BLINK Roppongi”)

name: BLINK Kioicho
card: Lounge and private offices on the 2nd floor of Tokyo Garden Terrace Kioicho, directly linked to Nagatacho Station
title: BLINK Kioicho — lounge seats and private offices in Tokyo Garden Terrace Kioicho, directly linked to Nagatacho Station
lead: BLINK Kioicho is on the 2nd floor of Tokyo Garden Terrace Kioicho, directly linked to Nagatacho Station on the Namboku, Yurakucho and Hanzomon lines. The official website calls it “a place that makes new ways of working possible”. It has lounge seats including semi-private ones, private offices for 2–8 and meeting rooms for 4–6. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: Directly linked to Namboku, Yurakucho & Hanzomon lines Nagatacho Station / Ginza & Marunouchi lines Akasaka-mitsuke Station, 2 min walk
Lounge seats (including semi-private seats) / private offices (2–8 seats) / meeting rooms (4–6)
concept: A place that makes new ways of working possible
The official website describes BLINK Kioicho as “a place that makes new ways of working possible”. Directly linked to Nagatacho Station, it is convenient for people on the move.
BLINK's second site after Roppongi, it has auto-adjusting lights, auto-locking doors and security cameras.
steps: The lounge is lined with seats, including semi-private ones.
With a stable internet connection and a multifunction printer, you can get work done on the spot.
Private offices come in rooms for 2 to 8.
According to the official website, they offer 22-hour access.
There are meeting rooms for 4 to 6.
They handle small team meetings and visitors.

word.title: What is Tokyo Garden Terrace Kioicho?
body: A mixed-use complex in Kioicho, Chiyoda City.
BLINK Kioicho is on its 2nd floor; the official website gives it as directly linked to Nagatacho Station and two minutes on foot from Akasaka-mitsuke Station.

credits: © Blink Japan G.K. (BLINK COMMUNITY official website: “BLINK Kioicho”)

name: H¹T Akihabara Chuo Kitaguchi
card: A site of 17 single rooms, close to three lines at Akihabara Station
title: H¹T Akihabara Chuo Kitaguchi — a corporate shared office with 17 single rooms and a meeting room for 8, on the 2nd floor of the Hasegawa Building
lead: H¹T Akihabara Chuo Kitaguchi, run by Nomura Real Estate, is on the 2nd floor of the Hasegawa Building in Kanda-Matsunagacho, a three-minute walk from the Central Gate North Exit of JR Akihabara Station. It is one minute from Exit A3 of the Tsukuba Express station and two from Exit 2 on the Hibiya Line. Seating is 17 single-person rooms and one meeting room for 8, and it is open 7:00–22:00 every day. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: JR Akihabara Station Central Gate North Exit, 3 min walk / Hibiya Line Akihabara Station Exit 2, 2 min / Tsukuba Express Akihabara Station Exit A3, 1 min
concept: An Akihabara site built around private rooms
Seating at H¹T Akihabara Chuo Kitaguchi centres on 17 single-person rooms. No open space or boxes appear in the official seat list, making it suited to calm work behind a closed door.
The official website describes it as a corporate shared office with no initial or base fee, usable for many purposes: remote work, a base for sales staff, seminars, training and interviews.
steps: Calls and online meetings can be handled calmly in a room with a door.
There is one meeting room for 8.
It can be used for internal meetings and interviews.
JR, Hibiya Line and Tsukuba Express
It is three minutes from JR Akihabara's Central Gate North Exit, two from Exit 2 on the Hibiya Line and one from Exit A3 on the Tsukuba Express.
Open 7:00–22:00 every day, it is easy to stop by early in the morning or at weekends.

word.title: What is the Central Gate North Exit?
body: One of the ticket gates at JR Akihabara Station, which also gives H¹T Akihabara Chuo Kitaguchi its name.
The official website gives it as three minutes on foot from this gate.

credits: H¹T (Nomura Real Estate Development Co., Ltd.)

name: H¹T Shimbashi Ginzaguchi
card: 12 private rooms open until 23:00 on weekdays, one minute from Shimbashi Station on the Ginza Line
title: H¹T Shimbashi Ginzaguchi — a corporate shared office with 12 single rooms open until 23:00 on weekdays, on the 8th floor of the SNT Building
lead: H¹T Shimbashi Ginzaguchi, run by Nomura Real Estate, is on the 8th floor of the SNT Building, a one-minute walk from the Shimbashi-crossing gate of Shimbashi Station on the Tokyo Metro Ginza Line, and three minutes from the Ginza Exit of JR Shimbashi Station. Seating is 12 single-person rooms and one meeting room for 6, open 8:00–23:00 on weekdays and 10:00–20:00 on weekends and holidays. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: Ginza Line Shimbashi Station, Shimbashi-crossing gate, 1 min walk / JR Shimbashi Station Ginza Exit, 3 min / Yurikamome Shimbashi Station Exit 1B, 3 min / Oedo Line Shimbashi Station, 4 min
concept: Private rooms in Shimbashi, open late
H¹T Shimbashi Ginzaguchi stands out for its long weekday hours, until 23:00. With 12 single-person rooms, it suits evening work or tidying up after meetings.

The official website describes it as a satellite-type corporate shared office run by Nomura Real Estate, with no initial or base fee, usable for remote work, as a base for sales staff, and for seminars, training and interviews.
steps: With a door to close, online meetings and calls can be handled calmly.
There is one meeting room for 6.
It can be used for small meetings and interviews.
One minute from the Ginza Line
It is one minute from the Ginza Line's Shimbashi-crossing gate, three from JR's Ginza Exit and the Yurikamome's Exit 1B, and four from the Oedo Line.
It is open until 23:00 on weekdays and 10:00–20:00 on weekends and holidays.

word.title: What is a satellite shared office?
body: A small workplace away from head office, for working while out or near home.
H¹T Shimbashi Ginzaguchi's official website describes it as a satellite shared office run by Nomura Real Estate.

credits: H¹T (Nomura Real Estate Development Co., Ltd.)
